A study’s package environment

John Ehrlinger

Source: vignettes/study-environment.qmd

Six months after submission a reviewer asks about Table 2, and you need the same numbers from the same code. Data and code are the easy part. The packages have moved in the meantime, because the server’s library changes whenever someone updates it, and nothing tells the projects that use it.

So each study keeps its own library, in its own directory, with every version written down in a lockfile. Start here covers setup(), which builds all of that once. This page is about living with it afterward: adding a package, updating one, answering a revision, and fixing what goes wrong.

What setup leaves in the study

File What it is
renv.lock The record: every package’s version, and each family member’s commit
DESCRIPTION The packages the study declares. A shared file, written by setup(), study_need() and study_declare()
.Rprofile Starts renv when the project opens
renv/settings.json The study’s renv settings, the shared cache setting among them
renv/library/ The installed packages

renv runs in explicit mode in our studies. The lockfile records what DESCRIPTION declares, not whatever a script happens to mention, so a stale template copy can never put a package into it. The other side of that bargain is that a package you install with plain install.packages() is not recorded until it is declared.

The library is shared too. setup() turns off renv’s per-user cache for the study, so the library holds real copies a teammate can read rather than links into your home directory.

Adding a package

For a package from the configured repositories, run this in the open project. It asks first, then installs the package, declares it and records it:

hvtiRutilities::study_need("cmprsk")

A package that is already installed is only declared, not recorded, so follow study_need() with renv::snapshot() in that case.

A package from GitHub takes three steps:

renv::install("org/repo")
hvtiRutilities::study_declare("repo")
renv::snapshot()

Run these in the console and keep them out of your jobs. Re-running a job should never install anything or change its environment.

Updating packages

An update is a decision about one study, so make it on purpose and record it. For one package:

renv::update("name")
renv::snapshot()

For the family, from a fresh session in the project, before anything attaches a member:

hvtiR::update()
renv::snapshot()

If the snapshot aborts over a missing dependency, pak has probably skipped a build-time (LinkingTo) package. Install the one it names with renv::install() and run the snapshot again. Do not rerun setup() for this: it restores the old lockfile first, so it can undo the update you have not yet recorded.

To see whether the library and the lockfile agree, use renv::status().

Bringing an active study on

The command is the one Start here gives, with adopt = TRUE. Two courtesies come first on a study other people are working in. If it already has a renv.lock, ask its owner before you run setup(). And warn the team, because setup() changes the library their sessions load from; they should close those sessions first.

A lockfile the study already has is kept. setup() restores the locked versions, declares every package the lockfile recorded and installs only what is missing. The exception is a locked version the family needs newer: by default setup() moves it, lists the move and records it. If the owner needs those pins held, pass upgrade = FALSE, and the run stops rather than moves them. Do not run renv::init() on such a study, which starts its library over.

Answering a revision

Open the project, on the R version the lockfile records, then rebuild the library the study was submitted with and check it:

renv::restore()
renv::status()

Then render the job as usual. If you need setup() on a study in revision, pass upgrade = FALSE, so that a package the install would move stops the run.

⚠️ hvtiR::status() does not check the lockfile. It compares what is installed with GitHub main, so a study held on its submitted versions is expected to show members as stale. That is the lockfile doing its job. renv::status() is the check that matters here, and running hvtiR::update() to clear the report would move the very versions you are protecting.

How the family is pinned

The family installs from GitHub main, so two people installing a week apart can land on different commits under one version number. The lockfile is what fixes that, because pak records the commit it installed from and renv reads that field:

"hvtiPlotR": {
  "Package": "hvtiPlotR",
  "Version": "2.8.6",
  "RemoteUsername": "ehrlinger",
  "RemoteRepo": "hvtiPlotR",
  "RemoteSha": "a4f3c9d8..."
}

renv::restore() then brings each member back at that commit, with no install steps of your own.

Common problems

Problem Fix
setup() stops before installing and prints a command You ran it inside a project whose renv is active. Close the project, then run the printed command from outside it
setup() says no study encloses the folder Open the study’s folder itself as the RStudio project, not one of its subfolders, and run setup() there; or pass root
“Could not solve package dependencies” Run hvtiR::doctor(). It lists the repositories R uses, warns on a dated snapshot and names any version floor they cannot meet
renv::restore() fails on a package that is not on CRAN Look for RemoteRepo in renv.lock. A package pinned on GitHub may need your own GITHUB_PAT
setup() warns that the study is set up without some packages They would not install, and jobs that load them stop. hvtiR::doctor() lists them and why; the logs are in renv/logs/ and the record is renv/hvtiR-setup.dcf. Rerun hvtiR::setup() to try them again, or install one by hand in the study and run renv::snapshot(). A family member that will not install stops setup() instead. The lockfile as it was is in renv/renv.lock.before-setup-<time>
An install fails reading a package in someone’s home directory The library holds links into a per-user cache. Rerun setup() for the study: it turns the cache off and replaces the links with real copies
A package is installed but not in renv.lock It is not declared. Run hvtiRutilities::study_declare("name"), then renv::snapshot()
renv.lock is behind the library renv::status() shows the drift, and renv::snapshot() records it once you have checked that it is what you meant
A teammate’s session errors just after setup They had the project open while the library changed. Restart the session
